 THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 16.11.2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 B.A.No.8775 of 2023  :3:
 ORDER Dated this the 16th day of November, 2023 Apprehending arrest in unknown crime No of Kundara Police Station, Kollam, registered for offences punishable under Section 420 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code, the accused have filed this application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
2. The prosecution case is that one Mr Nazar and his wife Asoors Beevi filed a complaint before the 3 rd respondent alleging that a marriage proposal was made with the 1 st and the 2nd petitioners to marry the daughter of the defacto complainant with the 3rd petitioner.
It is further alleged that as per the instruction of the defacto complainant, the 1 st and the 2nd petitioners to shift the residence to a big house on rent.
As the defacto complainant is the close relative of the 2 nd petitioner, and they had given Rs.10,00,000/- to them.
In the engagement, the petitioners' have given seven sovereigns of gold ornaments to the defacto complainant's daughter.
After four years, the defacto complainant and their daughter withdrew from the marriage proposal and married another person.

Thereafter, the defacto complainant demanded the amount spent by the for arranging the new rented residence of the petitioners' and the engagement expenses and also filed a complaint before the 2nd respondent.
The petitioners' herein also filed a complaint before the 2nd respondent against the harassment and threat committed by the defacto complainant and others.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the prosecution allegations were false and the offences against the petitioners would not lie.
It is further submitted that the petitioners had no role in the demand, collection, or refusal to return the amount, and therefore, they cannot be roped in as an accused 4.
I have considered the rival contentions.

5. It is seen that this Court had granted an order dated 18.10.2023, directing the petitioners to surrender before the Investigating Officer within a period of two weeks for subjecting themselves to interrogation.

It was also directed that, on such surrender, the petitioners shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that pursuant to the above order, the petitioners two and 3/accused Nos.1 and 3 had appeared before the Investigating Officer as directed and have been released on bail.
The said order was in force for a period of four weeks.

It is also submitted that Nazarudeen vs State Of Kerala on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79528898/

pursuant to the above order, the 1 st petitioner has not appeared before the Investigating Officer as directed by this Court.
In such circumstances, his request for anticipatory bail is rejected.
7. In such circumstances, this application stands partly allowed.

Pre-arrest bail plea at the instance of the 1 st petitioner stands rejected, and I am inclined to pass an order making the earlier interim order of the petitioners 2 and 3/accused Nos.1 and 3 absolute, subject to the following conditions:
shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer and shall appear as and when directed by the Investigating Officer.
